initialization.method: Fixed sources, every count/phase/layout, alternating policy order, serial replay. Coordinates, scores, initialization rounds, termination reasons and selected seed order must match exactly. Baseline numerical dependencies are checked against the reference commit.

browserKernels.method: Six actual uploaded masks. Both engines receive every original count/phase option with unlimited initialization deadlines. Independent source snapshots, warmup and three alternating-order timed rounds per image. Seed coordinates, errors, order, rounds and termination reasons must match exactly. Every selected seed mask is also compared pixel for pixel with the old exhaustive grid renderer. Initialization times exclude imports, input reconstruction, comparisons and hashing.

hunodan.criteria: Each prepare + solve + validate + export <=10 seconds; independent error <= that case’s validated release error, plus at most 1 percentage point for an identical pair; unchanged geometry, strict paper and substantial feature checks. Decode and independent external replay are timed separately.

features.method: Both colours; four-connected interior source regions with a solid core. At least 60% of each region must remain its original colour. Border regions and tiny or thin classification fragments are excluded.

weighted.method: Fresh automatic mask solves. Frames fixed before fitting. Checker strategy replaces the band; weighted strategy retains the original mask with zero band weights. Exported controls are independently rendered with resvg. Geometric and paper checks remain enabled. Variants swap both colours, translate by one source pixel in both axes with background fill, or alter only zero-weight pixels; the protected frame stays fixed.

Result capture and artifact writes happen afterward and have separate Node-clock durations. Version 1 solveAndConversionSeconds included harness capture and artifact writes and is not directly comparable.

profiles.method: The same HTTP profiling server supplies complete reference or current core snapshots. Exported function wrappers record inclusive and exclusive wall time. Every instrumented module plus grid.js and initialize.js must be delivered to both real workers. These are instrumented observations, separate from release timing.

timedVariation.note: The source masks and all coarse/fine grid attempts match. Later refinement checkpoints differ; the new final shared-cut proposal is rejected for adding one source-mask pixel. This locates a downstream variation, without proving that this gate alone explains every exported-mask difference.

limitations: The sweep relies on ordered samples produced by the positive-gap grid model. Arbitrary free curves retain independent polygon rendering.

The Node corpus times one call per policy per case, alternating order across cases. Browser kernel comparisons use warmup and three alternating-order rounds. Neither uses optimized cutting paths as input.
Exact candidate and mask comparisons isolate unchanged arithmetic. Fresh full solves have deadlines and may choose different valid checkpoints; all changed errors are retained.
Browser readiness measures DOM readiness of the enabled result button, not a paint timestamp; capture and file writes are excluded.
Node ten-second gates include preparation, solve, validation and export; decode and independent SVG replay are measured separately.
Instrumentation has overhead and can change backend calibration or deadline decisions; the uninstrumented release timings are reported separately.
